ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, C, D are on the same straight line, and D is to the right of C; A is above the base, triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle; point M is located on line segment AC, and line segment MD connects to point D on the right. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, put the straight line where the base is located on the x-axis, and take B=(0,0), C=(2,0). Because the side length of equilateral triangle ABC is 2, A is located on the perpendicular bisector of BC, with height sqrt(3), so A=(1,sqrt(3)) can be taken. M is the midpoint of AC, therefore M=((1+2)/2,(sqrt(3)+0)/2)=(3/2,sqrt(3)/2). Also because C is the midpoint of BD, and B=(0,0), C=(2,0), so D=(4,0). The base CD of triangle CDM is 2, and the height is the distance from M to the x-axis, namely sqrt(3)/2. Therefore the area is (1/2)*2*(sqrt(3)/2)=sqrt(3)/2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. From the diagram, place the collinear base on the x-axis with B=(0,0), C=(2,0), and D to the right of C. Since triangle ABC is equilateral with side 2, take A=(1, sqrt(3)). Because M is the midpoint of AC, compute M=((1+2)/2, (sqrt(3)+0)/2)=(3/2, sqrt(3)/2). Because C is the midpoint of BD and B=(0,0), C=(2,0), get D=(4,0). Then find the area of triangle CDM using base CD=2 and height equal to M's y-coordinate, sqrt(3)/2, giving area (1/2)(2)(sqrt(3)/2)=sqrt(3)/2.

method.method_draft: Use area comparison. From the midpoint condition C is the midpoint of BD, so BC=CD. Triangles BCM and CDM have bases BC and CD on the same straight line BD and share the same altitude from M to line BD, so their areas are equal. Now compute area of triangle BCM inside equilateral triangle ABC. Since M is the midpoint of AC, segment BM divides triangle ABC into triangles ABM and BCM with equal bases AM=MC on line AC and the same altitude from B to AC, so [BCM]=[ABC]/2. The area of equilateral triangle ABC with side 2 is (sqrt(3)/4)(2^2)=sqrt(3). Therefore [CDM]=[BCM]=sqrt(3)/2.
